study_identification_part.si_4_title: Resting-State Changes in Aging and Parkinson's Disease Are Shaped by Underlying Neurotransmission: A Normative Modeling Study

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: The study exclusively used the UK Biobank dataset. 25,917 healthy adult participants were included for normative modeling of brain function-neurotransmitter colocalization. Additionally, 58 participants diagnosed with idiopathic Parkinson's disease (PD) were identified for clinical deviation analysis.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "We included 25,917 adult participants from the UK Biobank not diagnosed with psychiatric, cognitive, or neurological disorders (Table S1) with known effects on brain structure and function as a control cohort. We also identified a group of 58 participants from the UK Biobank who were diagnosed with idiopathic PD (ICD-10, G20) before their imaging session."
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.location: Kasper2024.pdf.md: Methods and Materials / Cohorts, L43-44

answer.UK Biobank (HC, n=25,917): normative model construction and evaluation of age-related colocalization between brain function and neurotransmitter systems

answer.UK Biobank (PD, n=58): clinical research - testing deviation from normative aging trajectories in Parkinson's disease

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: The UK Biobank healthy control cohort was used to build normative models of brain function-neurotransmitter colocalization across aging. The Parkinson's disease subgroup was used to test whether and how functional changes caused by progressive neurodegeneration deviated from the nonpathological colocalization patterns. An age- and sex-matched subcohort (n=17,400) from HCs was used for regional comparison with PD patients.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "Normative modeling of colocalizations between brain function and neurotransmitter systems was based on the data of HCs. Regional differences in brain measures in patients with PD were calculated with respect to an age- and sex-matched subcohort of HCs." ... "Having established this reference for colocalization of normal age-related changes with different neurotransmitter systems, next we aimed to test whether and how functional changes caused by progressive neurodegeneration deviated from the nonpathological colocalization patterns."
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.location: Kasper2024.pdf.md: Table 1 caption, L57; Results / Deviations From Normal Colocalization in Manifest PD, L155-156

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: A single normative model framework was applied to model colocalization between three brain functional measures (fALFF, LCOR, GCOR) and 19 neurotransmitter systems. The model was built using all 25,917 healthy controls. No explicit train/validation/test split is reported; the normative model was constructed using the entire healthy cohort with Bayesian linear regression including age and sex as covariates.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: "We included 25,917 adult participants from the UK Biobank not diagnosed with psychiatric, cognitive, or neurological disorders (Table S1) with known effects on brain structure and function as a control cohort." ... "We modeled the co-localization level (i.e., the Spearman correlation coefficient) derived from spatial correlation analyses between neurotransmitter systems (n = 19) and individual brain functional measures (fALFF, LCOR, and GCOR) of all healthy controls."

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: The healthy control cohort (n=25,917) had a mean age of 64.03 years with SD of 7.5 years. Females (n=14,000) had mean age 63.5±7.4 years; males (n=11,917) had mean age 64.7±7.6 years. The age range 44.58-81.98 years was inferred from the supplementary methods describing the normative model prediction range. Separate train phase statistics are not reported as no explicit train/test split was described.

dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: The healthy control cohort consisted of 14,000 females (54.0%) and 11,917 males (46.0%) out of 25,917 total participants. Table 1 reports 'Sex, Male: 11,917 (46%)'. The female count and percentage were calculated as: 25,917 - 11,917 = 14,000 females; 14,000/25,917 = 54.0%. No separate train phase sex distribution is reported.
